title: dedicated-autoscaler-priority-routing-burst-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: customers on Dedicated fleets reported burst instability under prioritized routing: high-priority tenants could momentarily starve lower tiers and metrics lacked visibility into per-priority burst consumption. This PR introduces (1) priority-aware burst buckets and token-bucket smoothing per priority class, (2) routing changes so token borrowing is bounded and respects throughput guarantees, and (3) additional utilization and burst reporting metrics for fleet and per-priority telemetry.

Summary: implement priority-routing-aware burst controls and surface utilization reporting for Dedicated fleets. Changes include a new tokenbucket allocator that tracks per-priority tokens and a bounded borrowing mechanism, configurable smoothing window, API/config knobs for min-throughput guarantees per priority, and new Prometheus metrics + dashboard fragments.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement priority tokenbucket allocator and bounded borrow logic
- [x] Add config schema for priority throughput guarantees and smoothing windows
- [x] Expose new metrics: dedicated_fleet_priority_token_used, dedicated_fleet_priority_borrowed, dedicated_fleet_priority_queue_length, dedicated_fleet_priority_utilization_pct
- [x] Update autoscaler unit and integration tests
- [x] Add readable docs and console dashboard snippets
- [x] Backwards-compatible config parsing and default behavior

Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag `enable_priority_burst_v2`. Default off for 2 weeks; enable by customer opt-in. After canarying on internal test fleets we will enable for select customers, validate metrics and SLAs, then flip default on.

Backward compatibility: new config fields are optional with sensible defaults matching current behavior (single global bucket). If a customer does not provide per-priority guarantees, the allocator falls back to legacy tokenbucket.

Telemetry and dashboards: added Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboard fragment (docs/observability/dedicated_priority_burst.md). New metrics are exported with labels priority_level and fleet_id. Alerting rules suggested for sustained borrowed_token_rate > 5% over 5m.

How tested: unit tests for allocator edge cases, integration test that simulates priority traffic bursts and validates no starvation and that borrow caps are respected, performance test for overhead <1% p99 latency. CI includes a small end-to-end using a local dedicated-fleet simulator.

Related: ENG-1987 (autoscaler priority routing), SUP-4321 (customer incident), ENG-2040 (utilization reporting improvements).

release_notes: Enhancement: priority-aware burst controls and utilization reporting for Dedicated fleets. Adds per-priority tokenbucket metrics and configuration for throughput guarantees and smoothing. Backwards compatible behind feature flag.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated under runtime flag `enable_priority_burst_v2`. Recommended canary on internal test fleets for 72h and validate dedicated_fleet_priority_borrowed and utilization dashboards before wide enablement.
security_implications: no direct security changes; config parsing hardened and validated. No user-facing auth surface added.
qa_instructions: Run tests/integration/dedicated_autoscaler_priority_test.go and deploy the simulator with 3 priority classes; verify no priority starvation and borrowed tokens remain within configured caps.
changelog: Added priority tokenbucket allocator, bounded borrowing, per-priority throughput guarantees, and utilization metrics/dashboard fragments.
estimated_risks: Medium: allocator logic touches request routing and can affect latency under extreme burst; mitigated by feature flag and canary rollout.
customer_impact: Improves isolation between priority tiers and provides visibility into burst consumption. Default behavior unchanged unless customers opt into new config or flag.
